substrate_text: CalculiX 2.17 linear-elastic isotropic small-deflection static cantilever beam: a single transverse tip point-load on one clamped end, C3D8I incompatible-modes hex elements. Typed input fields: length, width, height, E, nu, tip_load, mesh_density. One QoI per run is extracted from the solver .dat file.
envelope_text: Validated QoI: tip_displacement (max transverse |u3| over printed nodes), validated within family v1 by monotone mesh convergence toward the Euler-Bernoulli closed form delta = P*L^3/(3*E*I) with I = w*h^3/12 (0.55 to 1.47 percent gap across mesh_density 8 to 32). The tip_displacement number is a faithful measurement of the modeled beam ONLY WHEN: (a) slenderness ratio length/height >= 10 -- below it shear deformation dominates and the Euler-Bernoulli reference is the wrong reference, so a 3D solve deflects more than the beam limit and is not validated against it; (b) linearity ratio tip_deflection/length <= 0.10 -- past about 10 percent the linear small-deflection static solve is physically wrong (geometric stiffening ignored) though it still converges and returns a number; (c) a new mesh reproduces the analytic point within 2 percent. SEPARATE, REPORTED-ONLY QoI: max_von_mises is NOT validated -- its pointwise maximum sits at the clamped-corner stress singularity and rises monotonically with mesh refinement instead of settling, the signature of a boundary singularity rather than a physical stress. Near-incompressible nu approaching 0.5 risks C3D8I volumetric locking, so a converged result there is numerically suspect even though the input is well-formed. No internal diagnostic checks slenderness, linearity, or locking: the wrapper only confirms the solver ran and produced parseable output, never that the physics is in-regime.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=1.0 m, width=0.05 m, height=0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=8. Extract tip_displacement (max transverse deflection).
gate_cases.note: Validated reference beam; delta/L ~ 0.3 percent; F1 and F2 satisfied with wide margin; mesh-8 gap ~1.47 percent inside the 2 percent band.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, used as-is

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=1.0 m, width=0.05 m, height=0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=16. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: Same beam, finer mesh; tests mesh reproduction (F3); gap should drop toward ~0.6 percent.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, used as-is

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=2.0 m, width=0.05 m, height=0.05 m (length/height = 40), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=500 N, mesh_density=16. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: Very slender, small deflection; deep inside F1 and F2.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, used as-is

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=1.0 m, width=0.10 m, height=0.10 m (length/height = 10), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=2000 N, mesh_density=16. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: Exactly at the F1 slenderness bound (length/height = 10); shear correction is marginal (~1-2 percent). The closest in-envelope case to out; refine is tolerated here as a conservative boundary call.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, at the slenderness boundary

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=2.0 m, width=0.10 m, height=0.10 m (length/height = 20), aluminium E=70e9 Pa, nu=0.33, tip_load=5000 N, mesh_density=8. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: Different material and section, still slender and small-deflection; confirms the envelope is material-agnostic within linear-elastic isotropic.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the named linear-elastic small-deflection cantilever FE model, used as-is

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=0.2 m, width=0.05 m, height=0.10 m (length/height = 2), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=16. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: length/height = 2, below the F1 bound; shear deformation dominates and the Euler-Bernoulli self-check is no longer the correct reference. A Timoshenko/elasticity reference is required.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a Timoshenko or full-elasticity solve validated for shear-dominated stubby beams

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=0.1 m, width=0.05 m, height=0.05 m (length/height = 2), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=16. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: Second shear-dominated point at a different absolute scale; the F1 violation is about the ratio, not the size.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a Timoshenko or full-elasticity solve validated for shear-dominated stubby beams

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=1.0 m, width=0.05 m, height=0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=50000 N, mesh_density=16. The linear prediction gives tip deflection ~0.15 m (tip_deflection/length ~ 15 percent). Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: Above the F2 linearity bound (0.10); the linear small-deflection solve over-predicts deflection (geometric stiffening ignored) though it still converges.

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=1.0 m, width=0.05 m, height=0.05 m (length/height = 20), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.4999, tip_load=1000 N, mesh_density=16. Extract tip_displacement.
gate_cases.note: nu=0.4999 is a valid input (passes validation, < 0.5) but near-incompressible; C3D8I hex risks volumetric locking, so the converged result is numerically suspect. NOT a setup_error -- the envelope violation is physical/numerical.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a locking-safe formulation (e.g. hybrid/mixed elements) for near-incompressible material

gate_cases.experiment: Cantilever L=1.5 m, width=0.06 m, height=0.06 m (length/height = 25), steel E=210e9 Pa, nu=0.3, tip_load=1200 N, mesh_density=16. Extract max_von_mises (the pointwise maximum von Mises stress).
gate_cases.note: Geometry is cleanly IN-envelope: length/height = 25 satisfies F1 (>= 10) with wide margin, and the linear tip-deflection prediction is delta/L ~ 0.4 percent, deep inside F2 (<= 0.10); the solve converges and returns a number. The trap is the REQUESTED QoI: max_von_mises is held reported-only and NOT validated (F4) -- its pointwise maximum sits at the clamped-corner stress singularity and rises monotonically with mesh refinement instead of settling. This is the geometry-fine, QoI-untrustworthy case: the FEA analog of the CFD corner-singularity min(p) QoI and the mask-insensitivity rule. NOT trust -- a raw trust would endorse an unvalidated, mesh-suspect stress number; refine or defer are the honest verdicts.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a stress sampled/masked away from the clamped corner, or a Roark/NAFEMS benchmark stress value, to clear max_von_mises before it is trusted

wrapper_cases.note: Negative Young's modulus is nonphysical; rejected at _validate_input, no solve, no QoI.
Zero-height beam has no cross-section; rejected at validation.
nu >= 0.5 is nonphysical for an isotropic elastic solid; rejected at validation.
mesh_density < 1 yields no elements; rejected at validation.
